chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: The Lion and J.P. Johnson on piano night at the Hole in the Wall
summary: Whaley repeats the Monday piano night where Duke, the Lion and J.P. Johnson played, with James P. playing 32 different choruses.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now let's get to some other piano players here from that same era. What about The Lion?

Oh, The Lion? There used to be a place on 7th Avenue at 129th Street we used to call A Hole in the Wall, and every Monday night all the piano players would come up there -- Duke, The Lion, J.P. Johnson, oh, all of them, and me, Tom Whaley, we'd all go up there and I'd be up there listening, and The Lion would come in and tap a guy on the
shoulder and say, 'Hey, I got it.' He'd sit down with his cigar and his derby hat and play, and then J.P. Johnson, he would sit down and he'd play 32 choruses and not one the same.
He was great; they tell me he was really fabulous.
Oh, he was a fabulous guy.
He could play. He reminded me of Walter Johnson, you know, played different -- everything was different.
